newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - December 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - December 4.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
SCAM TAINTED FORMER MINISTER EXPELLED FROM CONGRESS PARTY

Congress Chief Sitaram Kesri expelled former Communications Minister Sukh Ram from the party on charges of corruption. Sukh Ram's expulsion came as he obtained bail from a Delhi court. Sukh Ram was expelled after 360 million rupees in cash were recovered by the Central Bureau of Investigation from his residence in October.
The Times Of India
EX-FINANCE MINISTER FOR MORE STATE INVESTMENT IN POWER

Former finance minister Manmohan Singh has called more state funding in the power sector. He admitted the previous Congress government had erred in relying too much on private sector investments for the energy sector. He said the previous government's non-interest in additional capacity generation had adversely affected power generation in the country. The Congress government had cut budgetary allocations, expecting the private investments to do the job in the power sector. This, however, proved to be disastrous as the private power projects failed to take off due to lack of a clear-cut policy.
Financial Express
$250 MLN ADB POLICY LOAN FOR GUJARAT

The Asian Development Bank (ADB) is all set to clear the first ever $250 million policy-related quick disbursement loan for Gujarat. ADB sources said the loan would have three components, namely public finance reforms, state public sector reforms and infrastructure sector reforms. Sources said the loan would be routed through the federal government, which would also bear the exchange risk. With the $250 million loan to the state government, the total lending of ADB for India during 1996 would amount to $763 million, sources added.
BOMBAY BOURSE INDEX CRASHES TO THREE-YEAR LOW

Bear hammering by panic-struck speculators and institutional investors saw the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) index plummet to a three-year low of 2,798. The BSE index fell by 1,333 points from its previous peak of 4,131.22 points on June 17, 1996. The 50-scrip National Stock Exchange index touched its lowest level of 809.43, down 10.82 points from its previous closing. The declines in share prices were attributed to what dealers described as fear of the of unknown. Dealers blamed a move by state-owned banks to raise funds from the primary market as influencing the fall in share prices.
PRIME MINISTER REJECTS STATES' AUTONOMY IN POWER SECTOR

Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda has virtually rejected the demand of granting full autonomy to the states in the power sector. He said the presence of a central agency was essential to look after issues like fuel linkages and evacuation of hydro power generation and inter-state transfer of electricity. Gowda also said the federal government would play a role in determining tariffs particularly when a deficit state purchased power from a state with surplus power. The prime minister was addressing the chief ministers' conference on the power sector.
SLUGGISH DEMAND TO KEEP STEEL SECTOR IN DOLDRUMS

The steel sector is likely to remain in the doldrums for most of 1997 as a rise in production capacity at home and abroad may keep steel prices in check, said analysts. They said a slight rise in global hot-rolled coil prices to $290 per tonne from $260 at the start of 1996 would not help domestic prices rise. Indian steel prices were likely to rise by a maximum four percent towards the end of February, 1997 if the global rise continued. That, however would not be enough to cover a recent rise in administered prices, they said. A cut in import duty was another blow for the steel companies, analysts added.
The Economic Times
STATE PLAN ALLOCATION TO BE CUT TO CLEAR DUES

The cabinet has decided to recover dues, from the state electricity boards (SEBs) to the central power utilities by making adjustments in the state allocations during the Ninth Plan. This would be carried out in a time-bound programme. S. Venugopalachari, deputy power minister, said the decision had been taken to help the National Thermal Power Corporation, PowerGrid, Coal India Ltd (CIL) and Railways improve their financial performance, which had suffered due to non-payment of dues by SEBs.
STATE BANK PLANS $750 MLN FOREIGN EXCHANGE LOANS

The State Bank of India is planning to extend around $750 million in foreign exchange loans against its foreign currency non-resident (bank) deposits. The bank has also decided not to levy any penalty on corporates prepaying these loans. Sources said the decision not to penalise prepayment would make the loan very attractive to corporates as they could now leave their exposures uncovered even if they did not have foreign exchange earnings.
ADANI GROUP TO INVEST 20 BLN RUPEES IN CORE SECTOR FORAY

The Adani group's flagship Adani Exports Ltd is embarking on a 20-billion-rupee investment plan as part of its proposed foray into the core sector -- ports, power and industrial parks -- and petrochemicals. The investments are likely to be made over the next five years. A diversified export house into commodity trading, finance, agro and chemicals, Adani has incorporated six new companies -- Adani Port Ltd, Adani Infrastructure, Adani Power, Adani Minerals, Adani Petrochemicals and Adani Shipping -- for its proposed expansion plans.
MONEY MARKETS TO TIGHTEN IN SECOND FORTNIGHT OF DECEMBER

Money markets are likely to tighten in the second fortnight of December as the third instalment of advance tax payments will flow out of the banking system starting December 15, 1996. According to a debt market update, overnight money rates are likely to be in the double digit range as net outflows from the banking system exceed 30 billion rupees. The inflows are on account of coupon payments on various government securities and redemption of the 91-day and 364-day treasury bills. The outflows include advance tax payments which are estimated at 40 billion rupees.
Business Standard
CHANGES SOUGHT IN SHARE TRANSFER PROVISION

The Company Law Board (CLB) has asked the Finance Ministry to insert a clause providing for appeal in the pre-registration stage by investors whose shares were refused registration by the management of a company under manual share transfer. The CLB, emphasising problems faced by the investors in related cases of share transfer, drew the ministry's attention to the share transfer imbroglio between Sterling Horticulture and Resorts and Bharati Telecom (BTL). It said Sterling held nine percent of BTL shares, but had so far managed to get 1.5 percent of the shares registered. The rest had been refused registration.
APEX BANK SQUARES UP DOLLAR FORWARDS

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has squared up a substantial chunk of its $1 billion forward contract liabilities which were to mature in December and January. The outflow of dollars by way of squaring up has been balanced by the open market purchases of the greenback in the spot market. The bank is reportedly committed to crystallising all its outstanding forward cover position this time. The last time the forwards came up for maturity, the RBI had opted for a rollover in order to prevent the premia from appreciating.
The Observer
MINISTRY TO FLOAT TENDERS FOR OIL EXPLORATION SOON

The Petroleum and Natural Gas Ministry will shortly invite bids from private and public sector oil giants for speculative exploration of 200-250 small oil and natural gas fields. The directorate general of hydrocarbons under the Petroleum Ministry is currently preparing details for the tendering process following instructions from the government. The hydrocarbon fields to be offered for speculative exploration could be in the western and northeastern regions.
LENDING NORMS FOR NATIONLISED BANKS ON CARDS

The Reserve Bank of India will shortly announce prudent lending norms for the nationalised banks. The new norms would make it mandatory for the borrowing corporates to furnish an affidavit mentioning that they have not defaulted in paying the interests to any other bank or financial institution. The apex bank, which is worried about the increasing non-performing assets and large-scale corporate defaults, is believed to have prepared this set of norms to arrest the current trend, which has already created a flutter in the financial circle.
